project: Kumiki UI — ANAT5 Ming/Qing source-led Chinese ink character studies

sources.title: Twenty-five bust portraits of famous scholars — rightmost anonymous sitter
sources.creator: Unidentified artist
sources.medium: Ming handscroll; ink and color on paper
sources.view: three-quarter bust; rightmost sitter in IIIF image 161536

analysis.construction: The rightmost sitter has a tall squared dark cap, a three-quarter head turn toward image-left, a long narrow nose, lowered upper lids, moustache and a distinct tapered chin beard. Adjacent sitters are separate identities and must not be blended.
analysis.material: Fine dark contour lines sit over restrained warm ink-and-color washes; cap and robe use larger low-contrast masses.
analysis.microdetail: The cap edge is not a perfect rectangle; beard and moustache have separate roots and directional taper; eye openings are narrow and asymmetrical.
analysis.light: The face is modeled with quiet value changes rather than glossy highlights or strong photographic shadow.

crops.observation: Approximate normalized crop around the rightmost anonymous sitter; retain the tall cap, three-quarter gaze, cheek-to-jaw transition and separate moustache/goatee.
crops.implementation_rule: Use this sitter as the scholar identity source. Keep a distinct authored cap contour and face contour; do not average with the other two busts.

crops.observation: Approximate crop around the rightmost sitter's lower face; facial hair is attached to the upper lip and chin, with cheek and chin flows kept distinct.
crops.implementation_rule: Construct moustache roots, cheek attachment, chin mass and tapered individual fibers as separate semantic layers.

sources.title: Twenty-five bust portraits of famous scholars — comparative group crop
sources.creator: Unidentified artist
sources.medium: Ming handscroll; ink and color on paper

analysis.construction: Three distinct cap, cheek, beard and collar constructions are visible. Use as a comparison board only; no features are averaged into the canonical rightmost sitter.

sources.title: Woman at her dressing table — seated writer
sources.creator: Attributed to Leng Mei
sources.medium: Early 18th-century ink and color on silk
sources.view: seated figure; lowered inward gaze and writing-tool relationship

analysis.construction: The seated writer is distinct from the standing attendant: head inclined toward the writing surface, smaller facial marks, pinned coiffure and a clear hand-to-writing-tool relationship.
analysis.material: Silk support, restrained color washes, fine garment outlines and layered sleeve/collar overlaps.
analysis.microdetail: Hair ornament placement, hairline, lowered gaze, small mouth, collar overlap and the relationship between wrist, sleeve and writing tools.
analysis.light: Soft tonal transitions define the face and folds without hard glossy highlights.

crops.observation: Approximate crop around the seated writer's head and upper torso; gaze is lowered and head inclined toward the writing surface.
crops.implementation_rule: Keep the writer's gaze and head pitch tied to the seated-writing pose; build a high pinned coiffure with a distinct ornament rather than a generic hair helmet.

crops.observation: Approximate crop around the collar, sleeves and writing gesture; fabric overlaps the arm and hand rather than ending at a simple V-neck.
crops.implementation_rule: Use separate collar bands, sleeve openings, wrist/hand attachments and fold paths that converge at observed tension points.

sources.title: Woman at her dressing table — standing attendant
sources.creator: Attributed to Leng Mei
sources.medium: Early 18th-century ink and color on silk
sources.view: standing figure behind the seated writer

analysis.construction: The attendant has a separate head inclination, smaller compositional role and distinct position behind the seated writer. Head and neck must remain attached through the turn.
analysis.material: Fine contour work, subdued silk colors and overlapping robe/collar masses.
analysis.microdetail: A compact high coiffure with one dominant bun/pin arrangement, downward gaze, delicate facial marks and a narrower collar silhouette.
analysis.light: Low-contrast facial planes and garment folds; the attendant should not share the writer's face scale or hair mass.

crops.observation: Approximate crop around the standing attendant's head and upper body; hair resolves as one high tied mass with ornament, not two symmetric side coils.
crops.implementation_rule: Use a single high bun with a directional pin and asymmetric hair fibers; preserve the observed head inclination.

sources.title: Jiang Yun — Portrait of a Man
sources.creator: Jiang Yun
sources.view: full portrait; secondary tonal and robe-material benchmark

analysis.construction: A separate Qing sitter with a rounded cap, fur garment and different facial-hair identity; do not transfer those silhouette features to the Ming scholar.
analysis.material: Useful tonal benchmark for soft facial wash, layered fur mass and large robe volume.
analysis.microdetail: Observe cheek-to-jaw wash transitions and the way fur texture is grouped into larger masses rather than isolated noise.

sources.title: Jiang Jun — Portrait of a Lady
sources.creator: Jiang Jun
sources.view: full portrait; secondary female face and costume benchmark

analysis.construction: A separate Qing sitter; use only as a technique benchmark for delicate facial planes, hairline, ornaments and high collar.
analysis.material: Fine ink outlines, restrained warm washes and detailed textile patterning.
analysis.microdetail: Small eye openings, subtle lip definition, hair ornament and collar embroidery; avoid importing this sitter's identity into the 2024.180 characters.

sources.title: Portrait of a Lady
sources.creator: Unidentified artist
sources.medium: Ming ink and color on silk; available reproduction is monochrome

analysis.construction: Useful for head-to-robe scale, neck insertion, hand placement, sleeve volume and negative space only.
analysis.material: Monochrome reproduction; do not infer original palette from this copy.

sources.title: Court ladies and attendant
sources.creator: School of Tang Yin; formerly attributed to Su Hanchen

analysis.construction: Three women establish role hierarchy through different head tilts, garment lengths and spacing.
analysis.material: Aged, low-contrast reproduction; use for pose and contour only, not precise color measurement.
analysis.microdetail: Hair masses and ornaments vary by role; avoid giving all figures identical head silhouettes.

sources.title: Portrait of a man and his servant
sources.creator: Unidentified artist
sources.view: principal sitter and servant scale hierarchy

analysis.construction: Use difference in principal/attendant scale and garment volume as a spatial benchmark; no sitter identity is asserted.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Build the rightmost anonymous sitter's tall squared cap, three-quarter head silhouette and cheek-to-jaw contour as separate authored curves; ANAT1 is only the deformable understructure.
feature_targets.test_view: front and source-matched three-quarter head crops
feature_targets.source_observation: The rightmost sitter in IIIF image 161536 has a tall squared cap and three-quarter turn; the other busts in the scroll are not part of this identity.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Separate moustache, cheek attachment, chin substrate and tapered beard fibers; preserve source flow instead of a single pointed triangle.
feature_targets.source_observation: The selected sitter has a distinct dark moustache and chin beard; the scroll comparison shows other sitters have different facial-hair silhouettes.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Keep the seated writer's downward gaze, head pitch, face contour and neck attachment source-specific; use the Qing portrait only for subtle face/collar technique.
feature_targets.test_view: seated three-quarter face crop and neutral/expression frames
feature_targets.source_observation: The writer is seated and looking inward/down toward the writing surface; her pose and identity come from 2024.180.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Construct layered pinned hair and floral ornament over a visible hairline; collar bands overlap the neck and robe rather than forming a generic V.
feature_targets.source_observation: The seated writer has a pinned coiffure and ornament; the secondary lady portrait is a detail benchmark, not the writer's identity.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Use a separate standing-attendant head tilt and a single high bun/pin mass; preserve smaller compositional scale and head-to-neck attachment.
feature_targets.test_view: standing three-quarter head crop and full-figure scale view
feature_targets.source_observation: The standing attendant is a distinct figure behind the writer; the group painting is a role-hierarchy benchmark only.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Use overlapping collar, sleeve and robe masses with source-directed folds; preserve subtle wash edges and ink-line taper.
feature_targets.source_observation: The primary Ming/Qing scene defines each figure's costume; later portraits are only technique/material benchmarks.

feature_targets.geometry_rule: Maintain the seated writer as the primary figure and the attendant as a smaller, spatially separate secondary figure; keep all head/neck/body connections continuous.
feature_targets.test_view: full two-character composition and pose sequence
feature_targets.source_observation: The Met composition separates seated writer and standing attendant by pose, placement and scale; Smithsonian works are secondary role-hierarchy comparisons.
